messages:
sasha: Quick update — after the int4 bring-up of magnet-13b-compact I'm seeing weird repeated tokens late in the context (after ~28k). Short runs (<=8k) look fine.

anita: ugh. is this the new quant pipeline (bnb-int4 + per-channel)? :eyes:

sasha: yes, exact flow: hf-quant -> bnb-int4 stat-merge -> pack into shard. Ran on dedicated staging node (A100-80G).

devin: can you paste a tiny repro? even a short prompt that triggers at ~28k?

sasha: here's a minimal repro we used (trimmed):
```
# send a long primer (~29k tokens) then ask a Q
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "magnet-13b-compact-int4", "input": "<long-primer-29k>\nQ: summarize" }
```
Output starts reasonable, then at token ~28312 it repeats a 12-token span verbatim every 64 tokens thereafter.

kai: repeat as in the same exact 12 tokens repeated? might be kv wrap/stride bug or rope aliasing.

sasha: exact same token sequence, yes. not a simple loop like token-level degenerate sampling; it's a ghosted block.

anita: do we see same on fp16 or int8?

sasha: fp16 baseline on same node: clean. int8 small-precision build: clean. only int4 variant is affected.

devin: could be quantization export mismatch of RoPE freq table or position embedding stride. Any diffs in rotary scaling layer between quant and fp16?

sasha: ran a quick diff of rotary freqs from model_state dict before/after quant: L2 diff tiny but non-zero. attaching hash / checksum below.

ml-ci-bot: CI note: reproduced on staging with run id 2026-03-21-gnr-71. Collected tok-dump and kv-dump artifacts at gs://redwood-staging/kvdumps/2026-03-21/gnr-71\.

anita: good. can you run with kv-trace enabled and dump per-layer qkv keys for the repeating window? maybe something's being re-used incorrectly.

sasha: starting kv-trace now — command:
```
python tools/run_repro.py --model magnet-13b-compact-int4 --trace-kv --max-toks 30000 --out /tmp/trace.json
```

kai: also try forcing rope scaling mode to 'legacy' vs 'scale' in runtime config — if it disappears that's a hint.

sasha: tried legacy mode: repetition persists but shifts position (now at ~28400). suggests it's not just a frequency table but an index math problem.

devin: any inter-shard prefetching or circular buffer wrap logic recently changed in the int4 path? I remember a recent memcpy optimization for compact shards.

anita: yep, PR #1423 changed shard memcpy to use 64-byte aligned offsets for perf; there was a conditional that treats int4 packed bytes differently.

kai: that could produce misaligned reads into packed kv when stride not multiple of 64. For int4 we do nibble packing — a mis-offset would duplicate nibble ranges.

sasha: digging into the raw kv bytes, there are repeated 12-token patterns in the packed buffer as well. Looks like an overlap read.

devin: quick mitigation: revert the memcpy alignment for int4 path or add assert checks in dev branch to ensure unpacked length matches expected. Can you try a debug build that avoids the memcpy optimization?

sasha: built a debug runtime without the memcpy patch — repro gone on same artifact. No repetition.

anita: OK that's a pretty smoking gun.

kai: let's make a safety check in runtime: if model is int4/packed, don't do the 64-byte offset tweak or ensure we compute nibble offsets correctly. Also add a unit test that fuzzes shard offsets and validates kv roundtrip.

devin: file a rollback PR for the memcpy change and a follow-up that adds alignment-aware packing logic + unit tests. Tag security/perf owners.

sasha: filing PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2156 — revert memcpy tweak and add CI test referencing the repro.

ml-ci-bot: PR 2156 created. Benchmark job queued: perf/latency and correctness.

anita: follow-up: run a head-to-head quality check (ROUGE/BLEU) on a 5k long-context eval set between fp16, int8, int4-prepatch, int4-postpatch. Want numbers before we re-enable optimization.

sasha: will run overnight and post results. initial sanity: int4-postpatch should match fp16 on coherence metrics; int4-prepatch had huge coherence drop after 28k.

kai: also add a regression alert rule in Optimize so we get automatic signals when long-context coherence falls by >5% vs goldset.

devin: nice catch. glad it was an engineering alignment bug rather than RoPE math.

sasha: thanks all — I'll follow up with artifacts and the kv-trace diff when available. :thumbsup:
